summary: The P1 tests pass, but the Forge intake cannot honor missing-actor fallbacks or produce a renderable ForgeArt object.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] green: Missing-cast fallback fails after any Forge cast enables the Forge branch. prepare.mjs lines 314-324 omits unavailable actors, then Actors.tsx lines 103-117 calls staticFile(forge.cast[name]) without checking each actor. This breaks the specified Lily, Ben, and w04-family placeholder fallback. Rationale: the active intake contract requires mixed Forge and placeholder actors to render.

F2 [Blocker] green: manifestToForgeInput does not return the ForgeArt contract. prepare.mjs lines 269-275 returns absolute handoff paths and framesByGesture, but Actors.tsx and GestureInset.tsx require public-relative paths plus gestures, idle, gestureBox, and scenes (src/types.ts lines 22-40). Rationale: the adapter output cannot be consumed by the compositor.
nonblocking_findings: F3 [Major] green: The intake helpers are not wired to the production preparation path. scripts/render.mjs line 44 calls prepare(rel); prepareWithManifest is never called, and prepare(rel) rebuilds the spec from media/forge/manifest.json instead of the handoff copy. Rationale: invoking the normal render command drops the TSV intake result.

F4 [Major] green: T2.3 does not run an intake function; it copies two rows directly (tests/manifest-intake.test.mjs lines 83-105). T2.4 checks adapter fields but does not exercise prepareWithManifest or missing-actor rendering (lines 107-117), and T2.6 checks the manifest set rather than copied output (lines 127-133). T1.7 also checks the landscape bubble against portrait lyric and gesture boxes instead of checking box.portrait (tests/bubbles.test.mjs lines 151-154). Rationale: passing tests do not establish these specified behaviors.
